items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Yeah. Did you know Johnny Lawler used to be a butcher in the market? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, I knew of him.

ctx.x: Yeah, but they knew it. But they wouldn't have admitted. They wouldn't have admitted to public. As long as the fellow was bright enough to pass, they didn't care. See? But like you said, they wouldn't admit it. They would have admitted there, somebody said, well you playing that band with that nigger. You say, well I don't know he's a nigger. I mean, but he did know. But he said he did. He was covering up for his friends. That's right. That way they had plenty of them. What you say they had plenty of them done.…

Yeah. Did you know Johnny Lawler used to be a butcher in the market? Yeah, I knew of him. I didn't know anybody knew of him. Yeah, he used to be a trumpet player. And he'd tell me about how Arnold Macario would make a mistake, Macario. Yeah. He'd play a funeral in the afternoon and then could play a white job at night. At night, yeah. And get in trouble because he was a white job.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. Because, yeah. I knew that, for the reason they called me their name, because I knew this was too personal.
